newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - sluggish, awaits Dec expiry.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - sluggish, awaits Dec expiry.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market was dull this week with few spot sales, as the steep backwardation in the futures market left roasters unwilling to pay high prices for nearby deliveries, traders said.
With prompt supplies still hard to come by, the CSCE December contract maintained a hefty nine cent a lb, or nearly nine percent, premium to second-month March.
Most processors were expected to shun the market and scrape by from their own inventories until the December contract expires in two weeks.

"There is a timing battle going on," a trader said. "The producers would like to price against December. They don't want to give up the spread. But no roaster is going to step in and buy coffee against December unless they really need it."
The CSCE reported early this week that U.S. certified coffee stocks remained at a scant 321 60-kg bags, the lowest level since the CSCE began tracking stocks in 1980.
As of Wednesday there were 11,500 bags of coffee pending grading. While this was the largest influx of coffee in recent weeks, traders said it was still only a drop in the bucket.
